newsitem.title: JAPAN: Four die in landslide as Japan faces more rain.
newsitem.headline: Four die in landslide as Japan faces more rain.

text.p: A family of four died in a landslide in the latest tragedy caused by torrential rains while authorities on Sunday warned of more flooding in central and southern Japan.

The young couple and their two daughters, aged 2 and 4, were crushed to death when their home collapsed in a rain-triggered landslide in Takarazuka, near Kobe, 700 km (450 miles) west of Tokyo, a police spokesman said.
The tragedy came after 21 people died when a mudslide engulfed Harihara village on the southern island of Kyushu, 1,000 km (600 miles) southwest of Tokyo on Thursday.
A Meteorological Agency spokesman said torrential rains, which began on July 5 and have caused landslides and flash flooding on Kyushu and the main island of Honshu, were expected to worsen.
"Lightning storms and torrential rain will continue in south and central Honshu, including Tokyo, and heavy rain will return to Kyushu by tonight or early tomorrow," he said.
"Very serious damage may occur due to flooding and warnings have been sent out," the spokesman added.
Rainfalls in Kyushu may reach 1,300 mm by tomorrow, he said, adding:
"Nagasaki has already had around 850 mm of rain since last Saturday -- more than half the city's annual rainfall."

The freak seasonal rainstorms, which far surpass the normal rainy season, were due to a belt of rain clouds stretching south of Taiwan and another low pressure system from China converging on Japan, the spokesman said.
